writing.exampleCaption: Adding a variant breaks every match that does not handle it.
writing.explanation:
match forces every variant to be handled, so adding a new state turns every incomplete match into a compile error instead of a silent bug. Variants can carry data, which lets one type model a whole state machine rather than a bag of loosely related fields.

A boolean can distinguish two states, but it becomes obscure when a feature has several states or each state carries different data. An enum names the alternatives. `Message::Quit` carries nothing, `Message::Move` carries two coordinates, and `Message::Write` carries text. A value is exactly one variant at a time, so code cannot accidentally pair coordinates with a quit message as it might with a loose struct of optional fields.

A `match` examines the variant and binds only the data available in that branch. Every arm must produce a compatible type if the match is used as an expression. The compiler's exhaustiveness check is valuable during maintenance: adding `Message::Resize` points to every decision that now needs a policy. A wildcard `_` can be appropriate when all remaining cases truly share the same behavior, but it hides newly added variants if used merely to silence the compiler. For a small state machine, spell out the known cases.

Trace the sample with one value of each variant. Note that `Message::Write(t)` moves its `String` out when the enum is matched by value; match a reference, `match &message`, if you need to keep the original message. Then add a variant with a field and update the rendering match explicitly. This exercise connects data modeling, exhaustive control flow, and ownership. A well-shaped enum makes invalid combinations harder to represent and changes to the model easier to audit.

When the enum is public, adding a variant may require downstream users to update their exhaustive matches. That compile-time interruption is useful: it forces every caller to consider the new state rather than silently treating it as an old one.
writing.feedback: A catch-all removes the compiler's help exactly when you add a state.
